blocks.text: Aldehydes and ketones are oxidized to form carboxylic acids. Aldehydes are easily oxidized whereas ketones are reluctant towards oxidation because C-C bond has to be broken down during oxidation. Therefore, ketones are only oxidized by strong oxidizing agents, whereas aldehydes are oxidized by both weak and strong oxidizing agents.

Tollen's reagent also called ammonical silver nitrate solution contains silver ions in aqueous alkaline solution. These silver ions are readily reduced to silver metal on gentle warming with an aldehyde. A silver mirror is formed along the wall of the test tube. A dilute solution of the glucose (aldehydic sugar) was used to make mirrors for domestic use by means of this reaction. Ketones do not give this test.

blocks.alt: A round-bottom flask whose inside is coated with a shiny silver mirror.
blocks.caption: Figure 23.3: Only aldehydes give a positive Tollens' test (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 23.3).

blocks.text: Fehling’s solution is the bright blue Fehling's solution of Cu²⁺ ions in an aqueous alkaline medium, complexed with salt of tartaric acid. When warmed with an aldehyde, the Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to Cu¹⁺ ions, which in the alkaline solution form a brick-red precipitate of copper (I) oxide ketones do not give this test.

Aldehydes and ketones undergo substitution reactions by halogens readily at alpha position. Among aldehydes, only ethanal and among ketones, only methyl ketones possess the group CH₃CO- known as acetyl (ethanoyl) group. These compounds react with iodine in the presence of sodium hydroxide to form triiodomethane , a yellow crystalline solid called iodoform. Hence, the appearance of yellow precipitates will identify the presence of CH₃CO- group in the unknown carbonyl compound.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For acetone (propanone) the salt formed is sodium ethanoate, not sodium methanoate: CH₃COCH₃ + 3I₂ + 4NaOH → CHI₃ + CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + 3NaI + 3H₂O. Sodium methanoate, HCOO⁻Na⁺, comes from ethanal.

blocks.alt: A round-bottom flask of pale yellow liquid with yellow iodoform settled at the bottom.
blocks.caption: Aldehydes and Ketones having CH3CO group, whereas alcohols having CH3-CH(OH) group give iodoform test. Yellow coloured iodoform is formed in this reaction (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 107).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed box reads 'iodoform id formed'; it should read 'iodoform is formed'.

Ethanol also gives this test, while methanol does not. The reason for this is the presence of CH₃-CH₂-O, which acts as a methyl ketone-like structure (CH₃-C=O). Thus it can also form iodoform, and the test is positive for ethanol.
